title: The overflow detective
prompt:
A 32-bit add can go wrong in two different ways, and the flags record both:

- V (overflow) is set when the answer does not fit as a signed number: two positives giving a negative, or two negatives giving a positive.
- C (carry) is set when the answer does not fit as an unsigned number: a 1 carried out of bit 31.

The starter reads two integers into `left_r` and `right_r` and prints the report. Add them into `sum_r` with `adds`, which sets the flags (a plain `add` does not). Then point `ovf_r` at `str_yes` when V is set, and `carry_r` at `str_yes` when C is set. The conditions `vs` and `vc` test V; `cs` and `cc` test C. Keep the add in `w` registers: the same numbers added in `x` registers would never overflow.

With the sample input `2147483647 1` the program prints `2147483647 + 1 = -2147483648 (overflow: yes, carry: no)`.

## what is checked

- the report for the sample input
- the program exits cleanly
- the sum comes from `adds`
- the right report for other pairs, including 0 + 0, two negatives, and a pair that sets both flags
starter:
// add two 32-bit integers and report signed overflow and unsigned carry
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(left_r, w19)
define(right_r, w20)
define(sum_r, w21)
define(ovf_r, x22)
define(carry_r, x23)

.data
fmt_pair:   .string "%d %d"
fmt_out:    .string "%d + %d = %d (overflow: %s, carry: %s)\n"
str_yes:    .string "yes"
str_no:     .string "no"

.bss
.balign 4
left_m:     .skip 4
right_m:    .skip 4

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_pair               // read the two numbers
        ldr     x1, =left_m
        ldr     x2, =right_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =left_m
        ldr     left_r, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =right_m
        ldr     right_r, [x9]

        mov     sum_r, 0                    // replace these placeholders
        ldr     ovf_r, =str_no
        ldr     carry_r, =str_no

        // TODO: add left_r and right_r into sum_r with an instruction
        // that sets the flags. Then point ovf_r at str_yes when the sum
        // overflowed as a signed number, and carry_r at str_yes when the
        // add carried out of bit 31.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, left_r
        mov     w2, right_r
        mov     w3, sum_r
        mov     x4, ovf_r
        mov     x5, carry_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
